how: Row 1 is not a mutation: it is the failure the task was called to fix, on main's own files, recorded in the shape X14/X15 use for the organic kind. Rows 2-4 are the shipped tree with one source line changed (or one new line removed), the same `build-app.mjs` artefact the gates use, and the file restored before the next row. Every run is `harness:ios` filtered to Form.harness under an X29 lease on pair-a (simulator "nitro-ui A" / iOS 27.0, Metro 8295), so each filtered gate name satisfies nothing but itself. Logs: `node scripts/gate.mjs logs --branch task/X29-form-e4-pair-a`. Rows 1-4 are round 1. Rows 5-9 are fix round 1: row 5 is a mutation of the shipped witness, rows 6-8 and row 10 are the negative controls that decide what pair-b's `No view found at point (0.00, 0.00)` can and cannot mean, and a green run is written as one on purpose; row 9 forces the pre-fix aim ordering and lands on pair-b's other text. Rows 11-14 are fix round 2, on pair-b (simulator "nitro-ui B" / iOS 27.0, lease X29-cq1q0): row 11 is the app death behind pair-b's E4, reproduced on the shipped tree with the two provider answers this round replaces; rows 12-14 are the guards this round adds, and row 14 needed both halves of item 2 out at once to go red.

mutations.test: negative control N1 — is `No view found at point (0.00, 0.00)` what an aim the registry cannot resolve says?
mutations.mutation: after the case is green, press `{ nativeId: 'x29-no-such-view' }`: the native side cannot resolve the id, so it keeps the (0, 0) that `userEvent.press` sent (`HarnessUI.mm:248`) and hit-tests the window's own corner
redTests: green on purpose. An unresolvable aim taps (0, 0), this app has a hittable view there, and nothing is rejected — so the message pair-b printed is not "the id died", and "(0.00, 0.00)" is not a hit test before layout: the text formats the *arguments* `x, y`, not the resolved centre (`HarnessUI.mm:277`), so it reads (0.00, 0.00) for every `userEvent.press` that fails.

mutations.test: negative control N2 — is it a handle whose tree has gone away?
mutations.mutation: press the handle E4 took at its very top — before it waited for anything — after `cleanup()` and the positive control's render, with 1500 ms for the old tree to be freed
mutations.before: (the handle is not pressed after the tree changes)
mutations.after: await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1500)); await userEvent.press(pressable);
mutations.run: harness:ios:Form.harness — PASS, 15 of 15 (21.9 s), tree e2258ea093f4 — harness+ios+Form.harness-2026-11-12T06-32-30.672Z.log
redTests: green on purpose. A stale handle is silent, not an error: the registry's weak entry can still resolve, its centre is converted into the active window anyway, and the tap lands on whatever is drawn there. So a pre-wait aim can be wrong without saying so — which is the reason to re-aim — but it is not what writes the (0.00, 0.00) text either.

mutations.test: negative control N3 — is it a row the list has recycled out of sight?
mutations.mutation: scroll the Form 400 pt (`nuiTestScrollTo`, waited for with `offset > 100`) and press a freshly taken aim at `label-wifi`, a row the scroll has reclaimed into its section's holding view
mutations.after: need(forms.form).nuiTestScrollTo(400); await formReport(r => num(r, 'offset') > 100, …); await userEvent.press(await boxOf('label-wifi'));
redTests: green on purpose, and it narrows the field: on pair-a a row reclaimed by the list is still parked *inside* the window, so its centre hit-tests (onto a neighbour) and the symptom would be a press count of 0, not a rejection. For the rejection the aim's centre has to leave the window's bounds — the parked-row state of round 1's second bug, at the other end of the list, which is what pair-b had and pair-a has not been seen to have.

mutations.test: example/__tests__/Form.harness.tsx › E4 — the aim's own lifetime (symptom A, reproduced on pair-a)
mutations.mutation: the pre-fix aim ordering, forced: take the handle for `label-wifi` while its row is on screen, move the list 400 pt (`nuiTestScrollTo`, waited for with `offset > 300`, 400 ms for the settle), then press the handle this case took before the list moved
mutations.before: await userEvent.press(aim.pressable);  // aimed after the certification
mutations.after: const stale = await boxOf('label-wifi'); need(forms.form).nuiTestScrollTo(400); await formReport((r) => num(r, 'offset') > 300, …); await userEvent.press(stale);
redTests: expected +0 to be 10 — `expect(probe.log.pressable).toBe(10)`, and it is pair-b's second text exactly (`05:19:21Z`): the aim named a row the list had just reclaimed, the press went where that row's view now is, and nothing counted it. This is symptom A made to happen on pair-a on order, which is what says the two texts are one state and not two bugs.
